Then think about the scaling issues in the tragedy of the commons.

To build intuition, picture a figure of eight commons. 8 <- look it has a waist. This is a figurative commons, not a literal commons. So I don't have to explain why we don't just enclose it and benefit from having a single owner for each little field. But you might like to imagine that fencing is expensive. So we could build a fence across the waist at a reasonable cost.

That is the set up for the figure of eight commons. Now we can ask the question: what works best, two commons, North and South, managed separately, or one big commons? Answer: Single owner works best; we would have enclosed the commons if we could have afforded the fencing. If nature hands us a natural barrier, such as the waist of the 8, we use it. Two commons, North and South, with separate commoners courts works best, due to problems with scaling.

Now to double up the hypothetical. On Curmudgeon World, North and South embrace the idea of Population and Carrying Capacity Accountability Pools (PaCCAP). Perhaps the North fears that the South will neglect the soil, and end up sending starving people north. Perhaps the South fears that the North will neglect birth control and send surplus population south. Whatever. Both embrace PaCCAP and agree to ban migration. The North is one accountability pool and must take care of the soil and the carrying capacity of their land, and control the population to fit.
